# 08 Parse the timeline body once

## Outcome

The loop that drains a `timeline:` block's lines — skip blanks, call `parseTimelineLine`, collect
entries, collect diagnostics — is written once in `parseTimelineBlock.ts`, beside the grammar it
already owns. Three parsers call it.

## Why this ticket exists

Raised by the round-2 standards review. `parseTimelineBlock.ts` owns the *grammar* and its own
doc comment states the principle: "a second diagram kind gains animation by calling this, not by
growing a second copy of the grammar that drifts from the first one verb at a time."

The body drain was never extracted with it, so it exists three times — `parseFlowchart.ts:142`,
`parseClassDiagram.ts:880`, `parseSequenceDiagram.ts:665` — near character-for-character. Ticket
03 is what made it three, which is the moment the principle stops being theoretical.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `parseTimelineBlock.ts` exports a body-drain function (the reviewer proposed
      `parseTimelineBody(lines, startIndex)`; pick the signature that actually fits all three
      callers and justify it in your report).
- [x] **Completed later by ticket 10 (`f38fa30`).** All three parsers now call `parseTimelineBody`
      and none retains a drain loop. At the time of this ticket the criterion was overstated:
      **`parseFlowchart` still drained line by line**
      in its own loop, calling `parseTimelineBodyLine` rather than `parseTimelineBody`. Corrected
      after the final review pointed out the checkbox overstated the code. This is deliberate and
      documented in place: flowchart's loop re-checks the header, so a repeated `timeline:` is a
      no-op there and an error for the other two kinds. Unifying it would have been a behavior
      change. The code is right; this criterion's wording was not.
- [x] Every existing timeline-parsing test in all three kinds passes **unedited** — this is a
      behavior-preserving extraction, so a test needing a change means the extraction is wrong.
- [~] Diagnostic line and column numbers are unchanged for all three kinds. Class and sequence
      have diagnostic-level assertions; **flowchart has only entry-level line/column**
      (`parseSiren.test.ts:169`). The 48-parse before/after snapshot that proved the whole claim
      was a throwaway harness and is not in the repo. Corrected after the final review.
      Originally: assert at least one per kind, since the three callers compute `column` slightly differently today — check that
      before assuming they are identical.
- [x] The `sawError` / error-severity handling each caller does is preserved. If the three differ,
      say so in your report rather than silently unifying behavior — that would be a behavior
      change wearing an extraction's clothes.

The three parsers, through their source strings, as they are tested today.
